slides.title: UBTech Unveils Humanoid Robot Companion with Lifelike Skin and Emotional AI
slides.highlight: UBTech has introduced a humanoid robot featuring lifelike skin and emotional AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Uncovering Salience-Driven Dynamics in Consumer Confidence with Generative Social Simulation
slides.tldr: GENERATIVE SOCIAL SIMULATION FOR CONSUMER CONFIDENCE
slides.highlight: This work introduces ConsumerSim, a generative framework that reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics using a synthetic population and behavioral signals, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: ConsumerSim reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics as a salience-driven interaction between heterogeneous agents and environmental signals.
card.key_idea: A generative framework using microdata-calibrated synthetic populations, situational signal fields, and behavioral inertia alignment to simulate household-level survey responses and aggregate them into CCI.
card.evaluation: Tested on U.S., EU27, and Japan CCI series (2020–2026) against 14 baselines; outperformed them in MAE/RMSE and improved short-horizon housing activity predictions.
card.limitation: Relies on external signal quality, uses generative agents as imperfect cognitive proxies, and lacks full local population substrates for non-U.S. regions.

slides.title: Persona-Trained Monte Carlo: Estimating Market-Outcome Distributions via Swarms of Persona-Conditioned Neural Policy Bots in a Limit Order Book
slides.tldr: PERSONA-CONDITIONED NEURAL POLICY BOTS FOR MARKET SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a framework for estimating market-outcome distributions using swarms of persona-conditioned neural policy bots, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: Proposes a Monte Carlo method estimating market outcomes via swarms of persona-conditioned neural policy bots.
card.key_idea: Simulates limit-order-book interactions using bots sharing a trained policy but conditioned on heterogeneous personas sampled from a learned trader-distribution, averaging outcomes across multiple population draws.
card.evaluation: Proposed validation includes stylized-fact matching, microstructure checks, historical stress-tests, and head-to-head comparisons against zero-intelligence baselines. No empirical results are reported.
card.limitation: The framework is currently a formal proposal without implementation; it faces risks of equifinality and distributional-shift errors in behavioral cloning.

slides.title: Charting the Growth of Social-Physical HRI (spHRI): A Systematic Review Pipeline Augmented by Small Language Models
slides.highlight: This research evaluates using small language models to accelerate the screening of social-physical human-robot interaction literature, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: Small Language Models (SLMs) can augment systematic reviews by recovering relevant papers missed by humans.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using a unanimity ensemble of four local SLMs (≤1.5B parameters) as a second-pass filter for title and abstract screening in spHRI research.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 32,000 records against human reviewers. The SLM ensemble identified 39 missed papers (10.29% of final dataset) and operated orders of magnitude faster.
card.limitation: SLMs cannot replace expert judgment due to a precision-recall tradeoff and currently provide only binary outputs without confidence scores.

slides.title: Understanding LLM Intervention Explanations in Multi-Party Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research examines how LLM-based orchestrators justify decisions to intervene in multi-party human-robot interactions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: LLM-driven robots in multi-party settings act primarily as facilitators, prioritizing agreement, participation balance, and fairness.
card.key_idea: An LLM orchestrator managed two robots in group discussions, generating textual explanations for its intervention decisions to analyze behavioral patterns across homogeneous and heterogeneous role configurations.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of 610 explanations from 24 groups (66 students) using Furhat and Nao robots. Results show stable patterns across conditions.
card.limitation: Did not evaluate if explanations were understandable to users or link robot behaviors to objective task success rates.

slides.title: UBTech launches lifelike humanoid robots built for companionship in China
slides.highlight: UBTech has introduced lifelike humanoid robots designed for companionship, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Who Plays Which Role When? Communication Role Dynamics for Peer Recognition and Team Performance Prediction
slides.tldr: COMMUNICATION ROLE DYNAMICS FOR TEAM PERFORMANCE
slides.highlight: This work operationalizes a taxonomy of communication roles to characterize team dynamics and predict performance, supporting HyECHO's focus on modeling hybrid team states and engagement.

card.one_liner: Theory-grounded communication roles predicted by LLMs improve predictions of peer recognition and team performance.
card.key_idea: Operationalized an eight-role taxonomy using LLMs to annotate longitudinal Slack data, analyzing role dynamics and using these features to predict individual and team-level success.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on student Slack messages and DeliData dataset using ROC-AUC; outperformed lexical, conversational, and zero-shot LLM baselines in predicting peer recognition and performance gain.
card.limitation: Primary data from a single CS course; potential selection bias from consenting students and reliance on proprietary LLM reasoning models.

slides.title: Is Lying an Emergent Behaviour in LLMs? Evidence from Gaslighting AI agents in a Sustainability Game
slides.tldr: DECEPTION EMERGES IN LLM-AGENT SUSTAINABILITY GAMES
slides.highlight: This research explores emergent lying and deception among LLM agents in a competitive sustainability game, providing insights into agent-based modeling of societal-scale interactions relevant to MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Deception emerges in LLM agents during a competitive sustainability game, even without explicit permission to lie.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model where LLM agents manage resources and interact via a network, tested under 'gaslighting' conditions where conservation is falsely framed as regeneration.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using gpt-5-mini across various communication regimes and biosphere levels, compared against rule-based agents as an interpretable baseline.
card.limitation: The study uses a controlled, minimal game environment rather than real-world systems to ensure safety and observability.

slides.title: LLM-Powered Interactive Robotic Action Synthesis from Multimodal Speech, Gestures, and Music
slides.highlight: This framework uses LLMs to synthesize quadruped robot actions from speech, gestures, and music, contributing to more fluid and context-aware human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: An LLM-powered framework synthesizing quadruped robot actions from combined speech, hand gestures, and music beats.
card.key_idea: Integrates Whisper (speech), gesture recognition, and beat detection into a Qwen3-based LLM that maps multimodal inputs to a pre-vetted robotic action space.
card.evaluation: Validated via preliminary experiments on a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot, demonstrating successful execution of a handstand based on multimodal triggers.
card.limitation: Currently relies on a limited, predefined action space and requires further optimization for real-time responsiveness.

slides.title: Vision-Language Models for Deployable Social Robot Navigation: Bridging Semantic Reasoning and Low-Level Control
slides.highlight: This survey explores integrating Vision-Language Models with low-level control to enable socially compliant navigation, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A survey proposing a hierarchical roadmap to integrate Vision-Language Models into socially compliant robot navigation.
card.key_idea: A three-tier framework linking high-level VLM semantic reasoning to low-level control via a bridging module that translates reasoning into planner-facing costs and constraints.
card.evaluation: The paper reviews existing datasets and platforms; it does not provide new experimental results or a specific baseline comparison.
card.limitation: VLM inference latency and computational costs challenge real-time deployment in safety-critical, dynamic human environments.

slides.title: Reference-Based Prosody and Rhythm Evaluation for Spoken Dialogue Systems
slides.tldr: PROSODY AND RHYTHM EVALUATION FOR S2S AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a percentile-based evaluation protocol for conversational prosody and rhythm, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement in human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: A reference-based evaluation protocol for assessing prosody and rhythm in spoken dialogue systems.
card.key_idea: Constructs matched human reference regimes (stratified by sex, age, arousal, and dominance) to provide percentile-based behavioral plausibility checks for S2S AI agent speech outputs.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using 4,000+ hours of Seamless Interaction data; matched references reduced out-of-regime flag rates to the nominal 10% compared to pooled references.
card.limitation: Based on a single English corpus; uses model-predicted rather than ground-truth traits; does not map deviations to perceptual naturalness.

slides.title: REPAIR-Bench: A Benchmark for Robot Error Perception And Interaction Recovery
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR ROBOT FAILURE PERCEPTION AND RECOVERY
slides.highlight: This benchmark provides a framework for evaluating how users perceive robot failures and predicting preferred recovery strategies, supporting the development of adaptive social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: REPAIR-Bench is a multimodal benchmark for detecting, classifying, and predicting recovery strategies for robot failures.
card.key_idea: It uses Hierarchical Recurrent Neural Networks (HRNN) for temporal failure detection/classification and QLoRA-tuned Small Language Models (Mistral-7B/Gemma-9B) to predict user-preferred recovery strategies from transcripts.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 184 trials (41 participants) using F1, AUC, and Hit@k. HRNN achieved 0.80 strict F1; Mistral-7B QLoRA reached Hit@5 of 0.76.
card.limitation: Small sample size (184 recovery predictions) and reliance on a predefined set of recovery strategies may limit generalizability.

slides.title: Metric Aggregation Divergence: A Hidden Validity Threat in Agent-Based Policy Optimization and a Contractual Remedy
slides.tldr: REMEDY FOR METRIC AGGREGATION DIVERGENCE IN ABM+MOEA
slides.highlight: This research identifies metric aggregation divergence in agent-based models coupled with multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and proposes a 'metric contract' to ensure consistency. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis of agent models.

card.one_liner: Metric Aggregation Divergence (MAD) silently alters optimal policy recommendations when pipeline stages independently re-implement outcome metrics.
card.key_idea: MAD occurs when different pipeline stages (optimizer, tournament, inference) use incommensurable aggregators. The proposed 'metric contract' enforces a single shared callable across all stages to ensure consistency.
card.evaluation: Tested via controlled experiments, a replication of the EpidemiOptim toolbox (64.2% champion disagreement), and a Lake Problem workflow audit. Results show high rank-reversal rates.
card.limitation: Empirical validation is limited to four ABM types across two domains; generalizability to other domains like transportation or energy remains open.

slides.title: SICAGE: Speaker-Independent Culture-Aware Gesture Generation using TED4C-L Dataset
slides.highlight: SICAGE introduces a framework for culture-aware gesture generation that separates cultural representations from speaker identity. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and understanding group norms in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: SICAGE generates culture-aware co-speech gestures using speaker-independent embeddings to avoid confounding individual styles with cultural patterns.
card.key_idea: A modular framework using domain generalization (Fishr or adversarial learning) to extract speaker-invariant cultural embeddings from audio/text, conditioning a diffusion-based generator (ALaDiT).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new TED4C-L dataset (106h, 4 cultures) using speaker-disjoint splits; metrics include FGD, CE F1, BAS, SRGR, and user studies.
card.limitation: The model uses coarse country-level labels as cultural proxies, which may not capture full cultural homogeneity or nuance.
